name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
blurb: Badlands prairie where bison, prairie dogs and wild horses graze.

tip.title: Remove the prairie dogs
tip.text: Prairie dogs feed badgers, coyotes, rattlesnakes and golden eagles. Set Black-tailed prairie dog to -100% and watch the predators that rely on them.

sources.title: NPS: Nature and Science, Theodore Roosevelt National Park

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Theodore Roosevelt National Park, Black-tailed prairie dog, American bison). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A cool-season native grass of the mixed-grass prairie. Prairie dogs and bison both feed on it in spring and early summer.
A short, drought-tolerant prairie grass that grazers such as prairie dogs and bison eat.
A grey-green shrub of the dry uplands. Prairie dogs eat shrubs like sagebrush in winter, and bison turn to it when grass is scarce.
A low cactus of the open prairie. Prairie dogs rely on it for food and moisture in winter.
Reintroduced to the park. Mostly eats grasses and sedges, and its wallows are a form of ecosystem engineering that adds to prairie diversity.
Reintroduced to the park. A large grazing and browsing deer that is managed by park staff along with bison and horses.
Eats mostly grasses, plus prickly pear and shrubs in winter. Its burrowing mixes the soil and its colonies support many other species.
A fast prairie grazer and browser of open country, recorded often in the park area.
A browsing deer of the draws and breaks, common in the badlands.
One of several grasshopper species recorded in the park area. It feeds on prairie grasses and forbs.
A digging predator of burrowing rodents such as prairie dogs and pocket gophers.
A soaring scavenger that cleans up carcasses of animals such as deer and bison.
A flexible predator and scavenger. GloBI records show it eating prairie dogs, pronghorn, deer and elk.
A secretive big cat of the badlands that preys mainly on deer and elk.
A large raptor that hunts prairie dogs, rabbits and ground squirrels over open ground.
Drives the growth of the prairie grasses and shrubs.

story: Theodore Roosevelt National Park in western North Dakota covers 70,446 acres in three separate units, linked by the Maah Daah Hey Trail, with the Little Missouri River flowing through all three. Park officials manage bison, horses and elk to keep the ecosystem in balance.
matters: Roosevelt lived in the area after his mother and wife died hours apart in 1884. It is the only US national park named after a single person.
